analysis.title: CIO Views – Weekly Bulletin, Week 43: 19 Oct – 26 Oct 2026
key_insights: Central banks on hold this week lets markets focus on tech earnings. IT hardware producers across Asia and the US and one US hyperscaler report, testing the thesis that the AI capex outlook remains largely intact.

Eastspring's thesis from the prior week: higher financing costs may trim 2027-28 AI capex estimates at the margin, but growth is likely to remain rapid. Nasdaq and Kospi are down 6% and 21% from their October highs, which the authors say has priced much of this risk and reduced long positioning.

GPU rental rates for H100 and B200 racks have reached new highs, and rates for the six-year-old A100 have bounced back to late September levels. Eastspring reads this as encouraging for the AI capex outlook.

Google has increased the rollout of its AI agent framework announced October 8, which appears to respond to Meta's Muse release of September 8. Eastspring says higher consumer adoption should raise token use and compute requirements, and that the competition implies continued aggressive infrastructure spending.

Market focus is expected to be on growth in order backlogs for IT hardware producers, and on revenue and cash flow generation for hyperscalers. Eastspring agrees hyperscaler share prices likely trade inversely with credit spreads until AI revenues begin to catch up to capex.

The market expects the Fed, ECB and BoJ to hold rates at this week's meetings. Fed pricing rests on speeches by Williams, Jefferson and Daly arguing against a hike, and Warsh did not push back on them in a later speech.

The US 10-year Treasury yield fell from 5.3% in early October to 4.97% last Friday. Eastspring expects a Fed hold to shift Treasury risk back toward sell-offs and higher yields until the December 10 FOMC meeting.

Energy prices are rising on Middle East tension. Iranian attacks on ships in the Persian Gulf hit a new high of 28 this month, versus 16 in August and 15 in September. Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure add to the oil risk premium. Higher shipping logistics costs and risk premia have added about $30 per barrel to oil versus pre-war levels with output roughly unchanged.

Eastspring sees the risk that energy prices rise further. Press reports suggest the US will resume kinetic attacks on Iran after the midterm elections, and Houthi-Saudi fighting is seen as highly likely to escalate before any truce.

If energy prices rise further, the Fed not hiking in October could lead markets to see it falling behind inflation. The S&P Global US PMI prices paid index rose to a new cycle high in October, driven largely by energy and transportation costs.

US growth data are robust. Atlanta Fed GDPNow is 3.5% and Bloomberg consensus is 3.2%, against potential growth near 2%. Initial and continuing jobless claims are near cyclical lows, and the S&P US PMI Employment Index dipped slightly in October but stayed at its highest level since July 2022.

The risk Eastspring flags is that October and November employment growth is strong enough to lower the unemployment rate. U-6 underemployment has begun to fall, suggesting marginal labour tightening that could lift wage growth and add to persistent inflation.

Weekly market review: MSCI ACWI -0.9%, S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.7%, Emerging Markets -2.6%, Asia Pacific ex Japan -2.2%, Japan -1.7%. Gold fell 4.4% and the dollar index was flat. Global corporate bonds +0.1%, global high yield -0.4%, global government bonds +0.3%.

tension_points.bull_case: GPU rental rates for H100 and B200 are at new highs, A100 rates have rebounded, and Google and Meta are competing in AI agent products. Eastspring expects rapid capex growth to continue.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher financing costs may trim 2027-28 capex estimates at the margin, and hyperscaler shares may trade inversely with credit spreads until AI revenues catch up to capex.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weak growth in order backlogs at IT hardware producers, or weak revenue and cash flow at the hyperscaler reporting this week.

tension_points.bull_case: Fed speakers Williams, Jefferson and Daly argued against a hike, which drove the 10-year yield down from 5.3% to 4.97%.
tension_points.bear_case: A hold with rising energy prices, strong GDP and tightening labour data could make the Fed look behind inflation and send yields higher until the December 10 FOMC.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Strong October and November employment growth that pulls the unemployment rate lower.
